smt-2014-calculus-tiebreaker-02.title: Leibniz rule
smt-2014-calculus-tiebreaker-02.body:
By the Leibniz rule, with $h(x)=x^2+8x+20$ and $e^x$ (all of whose derivatives equal $e^x$): $f^{(100)}=\sum_{k=0}^{100}\binom{100}kh^{(k)}(x)e^x$. Only $k=0,1,2$ survive: $h=x^2+8x+20$, $h'=2x+8$, $h''=2$. So $f^{(100)}(x)=e^x\left[x^2+8x+20+100(2x+8)+\binom{100}2\cdot2\right]=e^x\left[x^2+208x+(20+800+9900)\right]=(x^2+208x+10720)e^x$.

**Answer: $(x^2+208x+10720)e^x$**

smt-2014-calculus-tiebreaker-03.title: Partial fractions
smt-2014-calculus-tiebreaker-03.body:
$\frac1{2k^2-k}=\frac1{k(2k-1)}=\frac2{2k-1}-\frac2{2k}$. So the series is $2\sum_{k\ge1}\left(\frac1{2k-1}-\frac1{2k}\right)=2\left(1-\frac12+\frac13-\frac14+\cdots\right)=2\ln2$ (the alternating harmonic series).

**Answer: $2\ln2$**
